title: Project: Entanglement Swapping
summary: Entangle two qubits that never interacted by measuring their partners in the Bell basis.
objectives: Combine two Bell pairs and a Bell-basis measurement to entangle qubits that share no gate
Choose the classically controlled corrections that give the same final state in every measurement branch
Quantify entanglement with the concurrence before and after the protocol
mission: Qubits 0 and 3 start in separate Bell pairs, (0, 1) and (2, 3). Entangle them without any gate acting on both: measure qubits 1 and 2 in the Bell basis and apply classically controlled corrections to qubit 3 so that qubits 0 and 3 end in |Φ⁺⟩ for every measurement result. Record c_before and c_after, the concurrence of qubits 0 and 3 after creating the pairs and at the end of the circuit.
hints: Create the pairs with qc.h(0), qc.cx(0, 1) and qc.h(2), qc.cx(2, 3). The Bell measurement on qubits 1 and 2 is the one from lesson 1.6: qc.cx(1, 2), qc.h(1), then qc.measure(1, 0) and qc.measure(2, 1).

The corrections are those of teleportation with qubit 3 as Bob's: apply X to qubit 3 if the bit from qubit 2 is 1, then Z if the bit from qubit 1 is 1, each inside with qc.if_test((qc.clbits[k], 1)): block.

Record c_before = float(concurrence(partial_trace(final_state(qc), [1, 2]))) right after creating the pairs, and the same expression again at the end for c_after. partial_trace removes qubits 1 and 2 and leaves the state of qubits 0 and 3.

prediction.question: Qubits 0 and 3 never interact, yet they end up entangled. What gives them this correlation?
options: A gate that the Bell measurement applies to qubits 0 and 3
The Bell measurement on qubits 1 and 2 projects the four-qubit state onto a state in which qubits 0 and 3 are entangled
The classically controlled corrections, which send the measured bits to qubit 0
prediction.explanation: The measurement acts only on qubits 1 and 2, but it projects the four-qubit state, and each result leaves qubits 0 and 3 in one of the four Bell states. The corrections on qubit 3 turn that state into |Φ⁺⟩. Nothing is sent to qubit 0, so its reduced state before the corrections is already maximally mixed and no signal can be read from it.

messages.ok: Qubits 0 and 3 end in |Φ⁺⟩ in all {total} sampled runs (with {outcomes} different measurement results), with concurrence {before} before and {after} after.
messages.wrong_size: Create the circuit as `qc = QuantumCircuit(4, 2)`: four qubits and two classical bits.
messages.forbidden_pair: A gate acts on qubits 0 and 3 together. The two ends may not interact: use only gates on (0, 1), (2, 3) and (1, 2), and corrections on a single qubit.
messages.measured_end: Qubit {qubit} is measured. Measure only the middle qubits 1 and 2, so that qubits 0 and 3 keep their state.
messages.no_measurement: The circuit has no measurement. Measure qubits 1 and 2 in the Bell basis (after qc.cx(1, 2) and qc.h(1)) and store the results in classical bits.
messages.branch_wrong: Qubits 0 and 3 are not in |Φ⁺⟩ in any of {total} sampled runs (worst fidelity {fidelity}). Check the pairs and the Bell measurement before the corrections.
messages.branch_partial: Qubits 0 and 3 are in |Φ⁺⟩ in only {good} of {total} sampled runs (worst fidelity {fidelity}). The corrections must cover every measurement result: X on qubit 3 for the bit of qubit 2, Z for the bit of qubit 1.
messages.no_record: Store the concurrences in the numbers `c_before` and `c_after`.
messages.before_wrong: c_before = {value}, but before the measurement qubits 0 and 3 are in a product state, so their concurrence is 0. Compute it right after creating the pairs.
messages.after_wrong: c_after = {value}, but the final state of qubits 0 and 3 is |Φ⁺⟩, with concurrence 1. Compute it from the final circuit, after the corrections.
